Lecture 25

Spinor tensor products and triality

Endomorphisms of spinors form a Clifford algebra, or its even part in odd dimension. As an orthogonal module this is a sum of exterior powers. In type DDD, chirality and duality decide which exterior powers occur.

Summary

The algebra End⁡(S)\End(S)End(S) is the Clifford algebra, or its even part in odd dimension. Hence S⊗S∗S\otimes S^*S⊗S∗ is a sum of exterior powers.

For BnB_nBn​, SSS is self-dual and S⊗S≅⨁k=0nΛkVS\otimes S\cong\bigoplus_{k=0}^n\Lambda^kVS⊗S≅⨁k=0n​ΛkV. For DnD_nDn​, the chirality element Γ\GammaΓ sorts degrees by parity and splits the middle degree. This splitting is the Hodge splitting of Lecture 23, with ΓΛ=cn−1⋆\Gamma_\Lambda=c_n^{-1}\starΓΛ​=cn−1​⋆. Self-duality of S±S^\pmS± depends on the parity of nnn. In D4D_4D4​, triality permutes 8v8_v8v​, 8s8_s8s​ and 8c8_c8c​, and it transports their tensor products.
